arxiv-1907-00270.title: An aggregate learning approach for interpretable semi-supervised population prediction and disaggregation using ancillary data
arxiv-1907-00270.creator: Guillaume Derval ✉, Frédéric Docquier, Pierre Schaus
arxiv-1907-00270.description: Abstract Census data provide detailed information about population characteristics at a coarse resolution. Nevertheless, fine-grained, high-resolution mappings of population counts are increasingly needed to characterize population dynamics and to assess the consequences of climate shocks, natural disasters, investments in infrastructure, development policies, etc. Dissagregating these census is a complex machine learning, and multiple solutions have been proposed in past research.

arxiv-2401-14875.title: Cohomologies, non-abelian extensions and Wells sequences of λ \lambda -weighted Rota-Baxter Lie coalgebras
arxiv-2401-14875.creator: Qinxiu Sun, Zhen Li
arxiv-2401-14875.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate cohomologies and non-abelian extensions of λ \lambda -weighted Rota-Baxter Lie coalgebras. First, we consider Lie comodules and cohomologies of λ \lambda -weighted Rota-Baxter Lie coalgebras. Next, we study non-abelian extensions of λ \lambda -weighted Rota-Baxter Lie coalgebras and classify the non-abelian extensions in terms of non-abelian cohomology group.

arxiv-2402-18519.title: Nuclear magnetic resonance studies in a model transverse field Ising system
arxiv-2402-18519.creator: Y-H. Nian, I. Vinograd, C. Chaffey, Y. Li, M. P. Zic, P. Massat, R. R. P. Singh, I. R. Fisher, N. J. Curro
arxiv-2402-18519.description: Abstract The suppression of ferroquadrupolar order in TmVO 4 in a magnetic field is well-described by the transverse field Ising model, enabling detailed studies of critical dynamics near the quantum phase transition. We describe nuclear magnetic resonance measurements in pure and Y-doped single crystals.

arxiv-2408-00927.title: Noise-Resilient and Reduced Depth Approximate Adders for NISQ Quantum Computing
arxiv-2408-00927.creator: Bhaskar Gaur, Travis S. Humble, Himanshu Thapliyal
arxiv-2408-00927.description: Abstract . The "Noisy intermediate-scale quantum" NISQ machine era primarily focuses on mitigating noise, controlling errors, and executing high-fidelity operations, hence requiring shallow circuit depth and noise robustness. Approximate computing is a novel computing paradigm that produces imprecise results by relaxing the need for fully precise output for error-tolerant applications including multimedia, data mining, and image processing.

arxiv-2501-00022.title: Algorithmic Idealism II: Reassessment of Competing Theories
arxiv-2501-00022.creator: Krzysztof Sienicki
arxiv-2501-00022.description: Abstract This paper explores the intersection of identity, individuality, and reality through competing frameworks, including classical metaphysics, quantum mechanics, and computational theories. Traditional metaphysical notions of fixed identity are challenged by advancements in cloning, teletransportation, and digital replication, which reveal the fluid and relational nature of individuality.

arxiv-2501-17071.title: On the sampling complexity of coherent superpositions

arxiv-2507-19408.creator: Sarah Lockfisch, Kristian Schwethelm, Martin Menten, Rickmer Braren, Daniel Rückert, Alexander Ziller, Georgios Kaissis
arxiv-2507-19408.description: Abstract Model multiplicity refers to the existence of multiple machine learning models that describe the data equally well but may produce different predictions on individual samples. In medicine, these models can admit conflicting predictions for the same patient – a risk that is poorly understood and insufficiently addressed.

Psoriasis is an immune-mediated disease with a strong genetic component that brings many challenges to sick individuals, such as chronic illness, and which has multiple associated comorbidities like cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, and psychological disorders.

pmc-11317149.title: Arabidopsis AGO1 N-terminal extension acts as an essential hub for PRMT5 interaction and post-translational modifications
pmc-11317149.creator: Andrea Martín-Merchán, Antonela Lavatelli, Camila Engler, Víctor M González-Miguel, Belén Moro, Germán L Rosano, Nicolas G Bologna
pmc-11317149.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Plant ARGONAUTE (AGO) proteins play pivotal roles regulating gene expression through small RNA (sRNA) -guided mechanisms. Among the 10 AGO proteins in Arabidopsis thaliana, AGO1 stands out as the main effector of post-transcriptional gene silencing. Intriguingly, a specific region of AGO1, its N-terminal extension (NTE), has garnered attention in recent studies due to its involvement in diverse regulatory functions, including subcellular localization, sRNA loading and interactions with regulatory factors.

pmc-11709465.title: Nanoscale imaging of pT217‐tau in aged rhesus macaque entorhinal and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex: Evidence of interneuronal trafficking and early‐stage neurodegeneration
pmc-11709465.creator: Dibyadeep Datta
pmc-11709465.description: BackgroundAdvances in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) have revealed a novel fluid biomarker, tau phosphorylated at T217 (pT217‐tau), in CSF and plasma, that predicts AD prior to cognitive deficits. Understanding the role of pT217‐tau is important in assessing efficacy of novel treatments aimed at early‐stage disease.

pmc-12398086.title: High platelet-to-red blood cell ratio and outcomes in trauma patients requiring massive transfusions
pmc-12398086.creator: Chi Peng, Yibin Guo, Fan Yang, Qi Chen, Lei Li, Faran Bokhari, Zhichao Jin, Shuogui Xu
pmc-12398086.description: BackgroundUncontrolled bleeding contributes to 40% of trauma deaths. While higher platelet-to-red blood cell (PLT/RBC) transfusion ratios may improve outcomes, the optimal ratio remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the threshold of PLT/RBC ratio and its impact on in-hospital mortality in trauma patients requiring massive transfusions.MethodsThis retrospective, multicenter study used 2014–2018 National Trauma Database (NTDB) data.

pmc-12410461.title: The CuPeR model: A dynamic online tool for predicting Cushing’s disease persistence and recurrence after pituitary surgery☆
pmc-12410461.creator: Guive Sharifi, Elham Paraandavaji, Nader Akbari Dilmaghani, Tohid Emami Meybodi, Ibrahim Mohammadzadeh, Neginalsadat Sadeghi, Amirali Vaghari, Behnaz Niroomand, Seyed Mohammad Tavangar, Mohammad reza Mohajeri Tehrani, Zahra Davoudi, Marjan Mirsalehi, Seyed Ali Mousavinejad, Farzad Taghizadeh-Hesary
pmc-12410461.description: ObjectivePredicting postoperative persistence and recurrence of Cushing’s disease (CD) remains a clinical challenge, with no universally reliable models available. This study introduces the CuPeR model, an online dynamic nomogram developed to address these gaps by predicting postoperative outcomes in patients with CD undergoing pituitary surgery.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 211 patients treated for CD between 2010 and 2024 was analyzed.

pmc-12552392.description: Eine Lungenseparation für thorakale Eingriffe ist in Abhängigkeit von der Altersgruppe mit unterschiedlichen Schwierigkeiten verbunden. Während die anatomischen, physiologischen und technischen Voraussetzungen bei einer entsprechenden Auswahl an Bronchusblockern und Doppellumentuben bei Kindern > 12 Jahren vergleichbar zu Erwachsenen sind, gilt dies für Neugeborene und Säuglinge nicht.

pmc-12800091.title: Placenta-derived extracellular vesicles in fetal health: emerging insights into brain development and environmental interactions
pmc-12800091.creator: Ethan Lewis, So Jeong Lee, Hae-Ryung Park
pmc-12800091.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Placenta-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are emerging as critical regulators of maternal–fetal communication during pregnancy. These lipid bilayer-enclosed particles, primarily secreted by trophoblasts, transport bioactive cargos—including RNAs, proteins, lipids and neurotransmitters—that influence a wide range of developmental and immunological processes. While much attention has been given to their roles in maternal adaptation and health outcomes, recent studies highlight their direct impact on fetal development, particularly fetal brain development.

pmc-13145696.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1732 DEVELOPMENT AND INTERNAL VALIDATION OF A CLINICALLY INTERPRETABLE NOMOGRAM TO PREDICT DISCHARGE FUNCTIONAL OUTCOME IN CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY–RELATED LOBAR INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE
pmc-13145696.creator: Yingjie Zhang, Yi Ju
pmc-13145696.description: Background and aimsPrognostic evidence specific to cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) related lobar intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) remains limited, our study aimed to develop a short-term prognostic model to provide evidence for long-term outcome prediction and to inform clinical care planning and resource allocation.

pmc-13157769.title: Foundation models in computational pathology: methods, applications and clinical implications
pmc-13157769.creator: Rasoul Sali, Yodit Aschenaki, Raymond Leveillee, Firas Baba, Liya Tessema, Christopher Dixon, Khaireddine Bachhamba, David Y Zhang
pmc-13157769.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The digitisation of histopathology has accelerated the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to cancer diagnosis and precision oncology; however, most deployed AI systems remain narrowly task-specific and difficult to translate across diverse clinical environments. Pathology foundation AI models are emerging as a unifying paradigm, enabling the learning of generalisable representations of tissue morphology through large-scale pre-training and supporting a broad range of downstream tasks.

pmc-13167146.title: Deep learning-based prediction of acute pancreatitis severity from abdominal CT with multicenter external validation
pmc-13167146.creator: Yanqi Xu, Brigitta Teutsch, Weicheng Zeng, Yang Hu, Shikhar Rastogi, Emmy Yuebi Hu, Isabella DeGregorio, Wan Fung Chui, Benjamin I Richter, Ryan Cummings, Julia E Goldberg, Edwin Mathieu, Belinda Appiah Asare, Péter Hegedűs, Kriszta-Beáta Gurza, István Viktor Szabó, Hedvig Tarján, Andrea Szentesi, R
pmc-13167146.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAcute pancreatitis (AP) is a common gastrointestinal disease with a rising global incidence. While most cases are mild, severe AP (SAP) carries high mortality. Early and accurate severity prediction facilitates management optimization.

pmc-13177381.title: How I Treat: Immune dysregulation in Down syndrome
pmc-13177381.creator: Melissa Gans, Matthew Wyke, Kayra Somay, Willa Thorson, Dusan Bogunovic
pmc-13177381.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Immune dysregulation is a common yet underrecognized feature of Down syndrome that contributes to infections, autoimmunity, and autoinflammation. Using clinical vignettes, this work highlights the underlying mechanisms and potential treatments for the immune dysregulation in Down syndrome. Introduction Down syndrome (DS) is the most common chromosomal abnormality found in live births, with an estimation of 5,000 babies born per year with DS in the United States (1).

pmc-13324660.title: Yes-Associated Protein Drives Helicobacter pylori–Induced Metaplastic Changes in Gastric Epithelium
pmc-13324660.creator: Byeong Min Yu, So Dam Lee, Bo Ram Hwang, Haengdueng Jeong, Jiseon Kim, Seokyoung Hwang, Minsoo Noh, Ki Taek Nam, Yong Chan Lee
pmc-13324660.description: Background & AimsHelicobactor pylori infection triggers a spectrum of metaplastic changes in the gastric epithelium; however, the upstream regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. In human gastric epithelial models, H pylori cytotoxin-associated gene A–dependent signaling stabilized and activated yes-associated protein, thereby promoting metaplastic reprogramming of the gastric epithelium.

HIIT improves oxygen consumption, body composition, and cardiovascular health, but its effects on the urinary bladder remain unclear.

pmc-13626889.description: BackgroundThe associations between ambient benzene exposure and thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism), as well as the role of biological aging, remain largely unknown.MethodsWe included a total of 385,130 participants from the UK Biobank, and Cox regressions were used to assess the association between benzene exposure and incident thyroid dysfunction. We employed restricted cubic splines to fit potential nonlinear exposure–response relationships.

pmc-13629116.title: Attendance and Academic Performance in Neurophysiology: Engaging Dental Students Through Active Learning
pmc-13629116.creator: Gustavo H Gameiro
pmc-13629116.description: Engaging students in foundational neuroscience courses such as neurophysiology remains a challenge in dental education. Class attendance is often assumed to be associated with academic performance, yet evidence in basic science disciplines is inconsistent. This study analyzed the correlation between class attendance and academic performance among undergraduate dental students enrolled in a neurophysiology course.
